I have created [`jump_analyzer.py`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mqsez_gb/jump_analyzer.py) (mounted at `/app/jump_analyzer.py` inside the container) and verified it against `/app/example_video.mp4`.

### How It Works
1. **Shift-Tolerant Background Subtraction**: Uses the first frame (which has no runner on the track) as a background reference and computes local eroded/dilated bounds (`cv2.erode` / `cv2.dilate`) with morphological opening (`cv2.morphologyEx`) to segment the runner while suppressing camera jitter and background motion.
2. **Trajectory & Jump Apex Detection**: Tracks the runner's horizontal median position and lowest foot position (`y_foot`) across active frames, locating the jump apex frame (`t_apex`) where `y_foot` reaches its highest point over the central hurdle region.
3. **Takeoff & Landing Frame Extraction**: Determines the takeoff and landing ground stance plateaus before and after `t_apex`, identifying the takeoff frame (`jump_takeoff_frame_number = 53` on the example video) and landing frame (`jump_land_frame_number = 62` on the example video) and writing the result to `/app/output.toml` using `toml`.
